requirements.note: British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules; no visa needed for a British citizen.

No visa and no immigration control — nobody's sovereign territory. But British nationals organising any activity here need a permit under the Antarctic Act 1994, administered by the FCDO's Polar Regions Department, not a visa. Joining a licensed cruise means the operator holds it.

American Samoa runs its own immigration and an ESTA is NOT valid here. Visa-waiver nationals are normally admitted for 30 days with a passport, onward ticket and proof of funds, but the rules are administered locally and change without notice. Verify before booking — this entry is the least certain in the app.
Outside the EU. Generally visa-free for British tourists on the same short-stay terms as other non-EU nationals, but not independently confirmed — check before booking.
Part of Finland: EU and Schengen, but GB is not EU. A British passport gets the ordinary 90-day-in-180 Schengen visa-free allowance here, the same as mainland Finland.
French collectivity outside the EU; EU-national freedom of movement does not apply to a British passport. Generally visa-free for tourism, but not independently confirmed — check before booking.

British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules; no visa needed for a British citizen. Entry is normally granted for up to 180 days, longer than the visa-waiver allowance most other nationalities get. Bring a return or onward ticket.
Bonaire, Saba and Sint Eustatius — Dutch special municipalities, outside the EU. Generally visa-free for British tourists, but not independently confirmed — check before booking.
A Norwegian nature reserve with no harbour and no airstrip. Landing needs Norwegian Polar Institute permission and happens only for research.
Inside the Australian migration zone, so British nationals need an eVisitor (subclass 651) just as for the mainland — GB is eVisitor-eligible.

Self-governing in free association with New Zealand, with its own entry rules. Generally visa-free for British visitors with a 31-day grant, matching the general pattern, but not independently confirmed for a British passport. A New Zealand NZeTA is confirmed needed for the transit through Auckland.
Outside the EU. Generally visa-free for British tourists on the same short-stay terms as other non-EU nationals, but not independently confirmed — check before booking.
Inside the Australian migration zone, so British nationals need an eVisitor (subclass 651) just as for the mainland — GB is eVisitor-eligible.

Entry follows Morocco in practice, since Morocco controls the populated coast including Laâyoune and Dakhla — so no visa for British nationals, on Moroccan terms. Gov.uk specifically warns solo travellers have been refused entry or turned back here in the past, on top of the usual Polisario-administered-interior caveat.
British Overseas Territory with its own immigration ordinance; no visa needed for a British citizen. A visitor permit for one month is issued on arrival.
Outside the EU and outside Schengen. No visa needed for tourism; gov.uk does not state a specific day cap for British visitors, so confirm before a long trip.

EU outermost region, but GB is not EU so freedom of movement does not apply here. French Guiana normally waives a visa for short-stay British visitors as it does for other non-EU tourists, but this is not independently confirmed for a British passport — check before booking.
Inside the Common Travel Area: a British citizen has full right of entry here, the same as in Britain itself. No visa, no ETA. Alderney and Sark are part of the Bailiwick.

British Overseas Territory with its own border control; no visa needed for a British citizen. Gibraltar is set to join the EU's border-free area under a 2026 UK-EU-Spain treaty, which brings EES and ETIAS to its land border with Spain — check gov.uk for the current state of that rollout before crossing overland.

Outside the EU and outside Schengen — a Schengen visa or the UK's own 90/180 Schengen allowance does not apply here. No visa needed for tourism; gov.uk does not state a specific day cap for British visitors, so confirm the length of stay with Danish authorities before a long trip.

EU outermost region, but GB is not EU so freedom of movement does not apply here. Guadeloupe normally waives a visa for short-stay British visitors as it does for other non-EU tourists, but this is not independently confirmed for a British passport — check before booking.
A visit permit from the Commissioner is required in advance, and is normally arranged by an expedition-cruise operator. There is no scheduled transport and no visa.
US immigration applies. The UK is a Visa Waiver Program country, so an ESTA is the route in — the separate Guam-CNMI waiver is for other nationalities.
An Australian external territory and a strict nature reserve: entry needs an Australian Antarctic Division permit, granted essentially only for research.
Inside the Common Travel Area: a British citizen has full right of entry here, the same as in Britain itself. No visa, no ETA — this is domestic travel.

Diego Garcia is a joint UK-US military base and the rest of the Chagos Archipelago is a marine protected area. A permit from the British Indian Ocean Territory administration is required and tourism is not permitted. Sovereignty is being transferred to Mauritius, which may change all of this.
Inside the Common Travel Area: a British citizen has full right of entry here, the same as in Britain itself. No visa, no ETA — this is domestic travel.
British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules; no visa needed for a British citizen. Entry is normally granted for up to 180 days, well beyond the 30 days most other nationalities get.

French side of the island, a collectivity outside the EU; EU-national freedom of movement does not apply to a British passport. Generally visa-free for tourism, but not independently confirmed — check before booking. Sint Maarten next door is Dutch and listed separately; the land border is open.
US immigration applies. The UK is a Visa Waiver Program country, so an ESTA is the route in.

EU outermost region, but GB is not EU so freedom of movement does not apply here. Martinique normally waives a visa for short-stay British visitors as it does for other non-EU tourists, but this is not independently confirmed for a British passport — check before booking.
British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules; no visa needed for a British citizen, normally granted for up to 180 days. Half the island is an exclusion zone around the volcano.

French collectivity outside the EU; EU-national freedom of movement does not apply to a British passport. Generally visa-free for tourism on the same terms as mainland France's third-country policy, but not independently confirmed — check before booking.
Inside the Australian migration zone since 2016, so British nationals need an eVisitor (subclass 651) just as for the mainland — GB is eVisitor-eligible.
Self-governing in free association with New Zealand. Generally visa-free for British visitors, but not independently confirmed for a British passport. Reached only via Auckland, which needs an NZeTA.

French collectivity outside the EU; EU-national freedom of movement does not apply to a British passport. Generally visa-free for tourism on the same terms as mainland France's third-country policy, but not independently confirmed — check before booking.

French collectivity off Newfoundland, outside the EU; EU-national freedom of movement does not apply to a British passport. Generally visa-free for tourism, but not independently confirmed. Most routes go through Canada, which needs its own eTA.

No visa for a short visit, capped at 14 days if you arrive and depart on the same ship (matches the UK government's own Pitcairn travel advice); a longer stay needs a Long-Term Visit Visa. Landing also needs a licence from the Island Council and there is no airstrip — the only access is by ship from Mangareva.
US immigration applies in full, so British nationals need an ESTA exactly as for the mainland — the UK is a Visa Waiver Program country.

EU outermost region, but GB is not EU so freedom of movement does not apply here. Réunion normally waives a visa for short-stay British visitors as it does for other non-EU tourists, but this is not independently confirmed for a British passport — check before booking.

Saint Helena's short-term entry permit is issued on arrival for a fee and is valid up to 183 days, per the UK government's own travel advice — you must show accommodation and a return booking. Ascension is separate and needs a 3-month visa arranged in advance; Tristan da Cunha needs the Island Council's consent and a ship, with no fixed day limit.

The Svalbard Treaty makes the archipelago visa-free for everyone, with no immigration control and no time limit. But you fly via mainland Norway, so you leave and re-enter Schengen — carry a passport. Jan Mayen shares the ISO code and is a manned station with no visitor access.
Dutch side of the island, outside the EU. Generally visa-free for British tourists, but not independently confirmed — check before booking. Saint Martin next door is French and listed separately.
British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules; no visa needed for a British citizen.
Crozet, Kerguelen, Amsterdam, Saint-Paul and Adélie Land. Access needs the prefect's authorisation and a berth on the supply ship Marion Dufresne. Not a visa question.

No airport: access is by boat from Samoa, and visitors need a travel permit from the Tokelau Liaison Office in Apia, which can take a month or two to process. No fixed day limit could be confirmed for non-NZ visitors, and access has been reported closed to visitors at times — check current status before planning any trip here.

Nine scattered islands and atolls — Midway, Wake, Johnston, Palmyra and the rest. Most are National Wildlife Refuges needing a US Fish and Wildlife Service special-use permit; Wake is an air force installation. Not reachable as a visitor.
British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules; no visa needed for a British citizen. Not the same place as the US Virgin Islands, which need an ESTA.
US immigration applies in full, so British nationals need an ESTA. Not the same place as the British Virgin Islands.

French collectivity outside the EU; EU-national freedom of movement does not apply to a British passport. Generally visa-free for tourism, but not independently confirmed. Reached only via New Caledonia or Fiji.

Northern Cyprus runs its own entry control and normally stamps a separate slip rather than the passport. Generally visa-free for British visitors as it is for other nationalities, but not independently confirmed — check before booking. Arriving directly (via Türkiye) counts as an illegal entry in the Republic of Cyprus's view; crossing at Nicosia does not.

Somaliland issues its own visas and does not recognise Somali ones. A visa on arrival at Hargeisa is the usual route, or one of the liaison offices in advance. Somali visas are not valid here and vice versa.

EU outermost region, but GB is not EU so freedom of movement does not apply here. Mayotte normally waives a visa for short-stay British visitors as it does for other non-EU tourists, but this is not independently confirmed for a British passport — check before booking.
